corridor_notes: GEM's segment name 'Yongchuan-Weiyuan Gas Pipeline' (zh_alt 永川-威远输气管道) does not match any independently found pipeline literally named 'Yongchuan-Weiyuan'. Two related, better-documented projects exist instead: (1) the trunk 'Weiyuan-Luzhou shale gas gathering pipeline' (威泸页岩气集输管道, aka 威江线/Wei-Jiang Line), 211.3km, Weiyuan Gas Station (Sichuan) -> Luxian -> Jiangjin Booster Station (Chongqing), fully operational 2023-04-23, the 5th 'gas-out-of-Sichuan' corridor; and (2) the 'Yongchuan-Jiangjin Shale Gas Pipeline' (永川—江津页岩气输气管道), ~64.5km, licensed 2021-08 by the Chongqing Fazhan Gaigewei (fzggw.cq.gov.cn), which builds one new Yongchuan Station and expands the Jiangjin Booster Station under the 'Chongqing Western Natural Gas Pipeline Network Plan' -- functionally the Chongqing-side leg feeding gas sourced from the Weiyuan block onward to Jiangjin, which likely explains GEM's 'Weiyuan' naming even though the physical line runs Yongchuan-to-Jiangjin, not to Weiyuan directly.
